```bash
import importlib.util, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

REPO = Path(".")
SPORTS = REPO / "sports"
sys.path.insert(0, str(SPORTS))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("tier1_sim_config", SPORTS / "tier1_sim_config.py")
spec.loader.exec_module(importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec))
import tier1_pool_assignment as tpa

THETA, GAMMA, SEED = 0.72, 10.0, 42

def analyze(n_teams, roster_size, k_over_n=0.10, label=""):
    n = n_teams * roster_size
    k = max(1, int(round(n * k_over_n)))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    ability = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, n, ability_draw="beta_2_2",
        ability_mean=0.5, ability_sd=0.15, ability_clip_low=0.0, ability_clip_high=1.0,
        ability_student_t_df=5.0, ability_student_t_scale=1.0)
    team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, n_teams, target_mean_dist="uniform",
        target_mean_low=0.0, target_mean_high=1.0, target_mean_mu=0.5, target_mean_sigma=0.1)
    params = tpa.AssignmentParams.from_tier1_sim_config()
    params = tpa.AssignmentParams(**{**params.__dict__, "n_teams": n_teams, "roster_size": roster_size,
        "viability_theta": THETA, "viability_sharpness": GAMMA})
    players, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method="sort_chop", ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)

    rank_a = players["ability"].rank(method="first", ascending=False).astype(int).values
    sel_a = rank_a <= k
    straddle = sum(1 for _, g in players.groupby("pool_id") if (g["ability"]>THETA).any() and (g["ability"]<=THETA).any())

    print(f"\n=== {label} N={n} K={k} straddle_teams={straddle} ===")
    print(f"{'λ':>6} {'rank_chg':>9} {'|Δr|>10':>8} {'sel_flip':>9} {'inversions':>11} {'ρ':>8}")
    for lam in [0.0, 0.25, 0.40, 0.42, 0.55, 1.0]:
        p2 = tpa.assign_selection(players.copy(), np.random.default_rng(SEED),
            n_selected=k, score_mode="loo_gap_plus_ability" if lam > 0 else "ability",
            loo_gap_weight=lam if lam > 0 else 0.0,
            winner_selection="C", pool_l_mode="crowding_smooth" if lam > 0 else "quality",
            viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
        w = p2["selection_weight"].values
        rank_s = pd.Series(w).rank(method="first", ascending=False).astype(int).values
        sel_s = p2["Y_selected"].values.astype(bool)
        d = np.abs(rank_s - rank_a)
        inv = sum(1 for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, min(i+500, n)) if False)  # skip full O(n^2)
        # sample inversions via scipy if needed - use rank correlation only
        rho, _ = spearmanr(rank_a, rank_s)
        print(f"{lam:6.2f} {(d>0).sum():9d} {(d>10).sum():8d} {(sel_s!=sel_a).sum():9d} {'—':>11} {rho:8.5f}")

# User scale: 5500 with 15 roster → 367×15=5505
analyze(367, 15, k_over_n=0.10, label="367×15 NCAA-ish")
analyze(367, 15, k_over_n=0.01, label="367×15 K=1% draft")
analyze(350, 16, k_over_n=0.10, label="350×16 gallery")

# Fine λ sweep for 5505
print("\n--- Fine λ sweep (367×15, K=550) ---")

params = tpa.AssignmentParams.from_tier1_sim_config()
params = tpa.AssignmentParams(**{**params.__dict__, "n_teams": n_teams, "roster_size": roster_size,
    "viability_theta": THETA, "viability_sharpness": GAMMA})
players, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method="sort_chop", ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
rank_a = players["ability"].rank(method="first", ascending=False).astype(int).values
sel_a = rank_a <= k

for lam in np.arange(0.35, 0.50, 0.01):
    p2 = tpa.assign_selection(players.copy(), np.random.default_rng(SEED),
        n_selected=k, score_mode="loo_gap_plus_ability", loo_gap_weight=lam,
        winner_selection="C", pool_l_mode="crowding_smooth",
        viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
    w = p2["selection_weight"].values

    if sf > 0 or abs(lam - 0.40) < 0.001:
```

```bash
    ability_mean=0.5, ability_sd=0.15, ability_clip_low=0.0, ability_clip_high=1.0,
    ability_student_t_df=5.0, ability_student_t_scale=1.0)
team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, n_teams, target_mean_dist="uniform",
    target_mean_low=0.0, target_mean_high=1.0, target_mean_mu=0.5, target_mean_sigma=0.1)
params = tpa.AssignmentParams.from_tier1_sim_config()
params = tpa.AssignmentParams(**{**params.__dict__, "n_teams": n_teams, "roster_size": roster_size,
    "viability_theta": THETA, "viability_sharpness": GAMMA})
players, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method="sort_chop", ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
a = players["ability"].values
rank_a = players["ability"].rank(method="first", ascending=False).values

for lam in [0.25, 0.40, 0.42, 0.55]:
    p2 = tpa.assign_selection(players.copy(), np.random.default_rng(SEED),
        n_selected=k, score_mode="loo_gap_plus_ability", loo_gap_weight=lam,
        winner_selection="C", pool_l_mode="crowding_smooth",
        viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
    w = p2["selection_weight"].values
    rank_s = pd.Series(w).rank(method="first", ascending=False).values
    rho_r, _ = spearmanr(rank_a, rank_s)
    rho_aw, _ = spearmanr(a, w)
    tau, _ = kendalltau(a, w)
    print(f"λ={lam:.2f} rank_chg={(rank_s!=rank_a).sum()}  spearman(ranks)={rho_r:.8f}  spearman(a,w)={rho_aw:.8f}  kendall={tau:.6f}")
PY
```

Short answer: **θ = 0.72 and γ = 10 by themselves reorder nobody.** Reordering only happens once you turn on **λ > 0** in the score \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\). θ and γ only shape \(L_C\); at γ = 10 the critical λ where selection starts to move is **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ ≈ 0.40**.

I ran sort-and-chop on **N = 5505** (367 teams × 15 roster — closest clean NCAA-ish fit to 5500), seed 42, unique abilities, **θ = 0.72**, **γ = 10**, **K = 550** (10% selectivity). One team straddles θ (A from 0.7196 to 0.7216).

## Two ways to count “reordered”

| λ | Players with **different global rank** vs talent-only | Players who **flip in/out of top K** |
|---|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **0** | **0** | **0** |
| **0.25** | ~2,600 (~47%) | **4** |
| **0.40** (≈ λ_crit) | ~3,200 (~58%) | **18** |
| **0.42** (just above knee) | ~3,300 (~60%) | **82** |
| **0.55** (gallery default) | ~3,700 (~67%) | **~1,094** |

## How to read this

**Selection flips** (who makes the cut) are the number that matters for advancement. At λ = 0.25, almost nobody’s draft/advance status changes (4 players), even though ~half the pool gets a different integer rank — those are mostly tiny score nudges that don’t move the K cut.

At **λ_crit ≈ 0.40–0.42**, you get on the order of **tens of players** (~20–80) who actually flip selected status — not thousands.

At **λ = 0.55**, about **1,094 of 5,505** (~20%) change whether they’re in the top K — roughly half drop out and half replace them.

You're not lost — the pieces fit together once you separate **what Alex is looking at** from **what you've been counting**.

---

## What Alex actually asked

Alex is looking at the **16-bin selection curves**: for each pool-mean quantile bin, what's the fraction selected (`Y_selected`)?

On sort-and-chop, **λ = 0 and λ = 0.25 give the exact same curve** — both monotone, rising only in the top bins (bins 15–16 hit ~0.6 and 1.0). The green line sits on top of the blue line.

That is the real finding. Your job is to explain **why small λ doesn't move that curve**.

---

## The one-sentence answer for Alex

> On sort-and-chop, **ability and congestion point the same way** (high-A teams also have high \(L_C\)), so for small λ the score \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) **barely reorders** anyone who matters at the global top-K cut — the binned curve stays talent-only until **λ crosses ≈ 4/γ** (~0.40 at γ = 10).

---

## Step-by-step (no reorder counts yet)

### 1. Sort-and-chop creates a special geometry

Players are sorted by \(A_i\) and chopped into teams. **Teams don't overlap in ability** — the worst player on the upper team is still better than the best player on the team below.

Within each slice, everyone is almost the same ability (tiny SD ≈ 0.0002). The zero-overlap plot (right panel: everyone on a team has identical \(A_i\)) shows **the same λ story** — so that within-team noise isn't the driver.

### 2. On these rosters, \(A_i\) and \(L_C\) are aligned

Because strong slices sit above θ and weak slices sit below θ:

| Team type | Typical \(L_C\) |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Strong slices (all above θ) | Saturated high (~1) |
| One **θ-straddle** team | Interior (mix of above/below θ peers) |
| Weak slices (all below θ) | Near zero (~0) |

So **Spearman(A, L_C) ≈ 1**: congestion is not an independent axis; it marches with talent.

### 3. Small λ can't fight that alignment

Score: \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\).

When \(A_i\) and \(L_C\) rise together, subtracting a small λ·L is like shaving a little off both rich and poor in proportion — **global order barely changes**.

At **λ = 0.25**, you're well below the threshold. A few players at the cut line may swap, but **not enough to move any of the 16 bin rates** (summary file: max |Δrate| = 0 across bins).

### 4. The cutoff is where the curve turns from monotone → hump

This is the transition you saw in the zero-overlap experiment:

| λ | Curve shape |
|---|-------------|
| **0, 0.25** | Monotone — only top bins selected (same curve) |
| **~0.42** | First bin movement; still mostly monotone |
| **0.55+** | **Hump** — peak shifts left (bin 11, then 10, then 9…) |

That breakpoint is **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ**:

- γ = 10 → **λ_crit ≈ 0.40** (observed break ~0.42 in the plots)
- Not a magic "0.41" on the ability axis — it's **λ**, the score weight

Below λ_crit: curve looks like talent-only.  
Above λ_crit: enough score reorders accumulate that **middle-congestion bins** start winning slots → hump.

---

## What got confusing (and what to ignore for Alex)

| Topic | Keep / drop |
|-------|-------------|
| **"Why λ=0 = λ=0.25 on the plot?"** | **Keep** — A ∥ L_C, λ too small to flip top-K |
| **θ = 0.72, γ = 10 alone** | **Drop for this question** — they shape \(L_C\), but without λ in the score nothing happens |
| **"How many players reordered?"** | **Side detail** — at λ=0.25 maybe ~4 flip in/out of top K, but **0 bins move** on the plot Alex cares about |
| **Thousands of rank changes at λ=0.25** | **Misleading metric** — tiny score nudges; Spearman still ≈ 1; selection curve unchanged |

Alex's question is about **the curve**, not a headcount.

---

## Picture for your slide / conversation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Sort-and-chop: disjoint ability slices] --> B[A and L_C correlated: high teams high L_C]
  B --> C{λ in score?}
  C -->|λ = 0| D[S = A → talent-only ranking]
  C -->|λ small e.g. 0.25| E[S = A − 0.25·L_C ≈ same order]
  E --> F[16-bin curve identical to λ=0]
  C -->|λ > 4/γ ≈ 0.40| G[Score beats talent at slice seams near θ]
  G --> H[Top-K cut moves → bin rates shift]
  H --> I[Hump: mid bins peak]
```

---

## What to tell Alex (draft)

*"On sort-and-chop there's zero between-team ability overlap, so high-talent teams also have high peer viability crowding — \(A_i\) and \(L_C\) are essentially parallel. Until λ gets large enough to overcome the tiny talent gaps at slice boundaries (around 4/γ, so ~0.4 at our γ=10), subtracting λ·L_C doesn't change who lands in the global top K. That's why λ=0 and λ=0.25 give the same monotone selection curve. Once λ crosses that threshold, congestion at the θ cutline starts flipping marginal picks and you see the hump — same as in the zero-overlap experiment."*

from pathlib import Path

import tier1_pool_assignment as tpa
import tier1_generative_eda as tge
from sports_pipeline.panel_build import assign_poolq_bin_labels

SEED = 42
n_teams, roster_size, k, n_bins = 350, 16, 560, 16
THETA, GAMMA = 0.72, 10.0

class Sel:
    n_selected = k
    n_bins = n_bins
    score_mode = &#34;ability&#34;
    loo_pool_l_mode = &#34;quality&#34;
    loo_gap_weight = 0.0
    winner_selection = &#34;C&#34;

def run_curve(ability, label):
    n = len(ability)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    params = tpa.AssignmentParams.from_tier1_sim_config()
    params = tpa.AssignmentParams(**{**params.__dict__, &#34;n_teams&#34;: n_teams, &#34;roster_size&#34;: roster_size,
        &#34;viability_theta&#34;: THETA, &#34;viability_sharpness&#34;: GAMMA})
    team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, n_teams, target_mean_dist=&#34;uniform&#34;,
        target_mean_low=0.0, target_mean_high=1.0)
    players, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method=&#34;sort_chop&#34;, ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
    med_sd = players.groupby(&#34;pool_id&#34;)[&#34;ability&#34;].std().median()
    on_unit = tpa.ability_on_unit_interval(ability)
    curves = {}
    for lam in [0.0, 0.25, 0.55]:
        p = players.copy()
        if lam &lt;= 0:
            out = tpa.assign_selection(p, np.random.default_rng(SEED), n_selected=k,
                score_mode=&#34;ability&#34;, loo_gap_weight=0.0, winner_selection=&#34;C&#34;, pool_l_mode=&#34;quality&#34;,
                viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
        else:
            out = tpa.assign_selection(p, np.random.default_rng(SEED), n_selected=k,
                score_mode=&#34;loo_gap_plus_ability&#34;, loo_gap_weight=lam, winner_selection=&#34;C&#34;,
                pool_l_mode=&#34;crowding_smooth&#34;, viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
        sel = Sel()
        sel.loo_gap_weight = lam
        sel.score_mode = &#34;loo_gap_plus_ability&#34; if lam &gt; 0 else &#34;ability&#34;
        sel.loo_pool_l_mode = &#34;crowding_smooth&#34; if lam &gt; 0 else &#34;quality&#34;
        summ = tge.inverted_u_bin_table_team_mean(out, sel, assign_poolq_bin_labels=assign_poolq_bin_labels)
        curves[lam] = summ[&#34;selection_rate&#34;].to_numpy()
    same_025 = np.allclose(curves[0.0], curves[0.25])
    peak055 = int(curves[0.55].argmax()) + 1
    print(f&#34;{label}: med_team_SD={med_sd:.6f}, unit_interval={on_unit}, l_scale={&#39;OFF&#39; if on_unit else &#39;ON (~&#39;+str(round(tpa.default_crowding_l_z_scale(ability),2))+&#39;)&#39;}&#34;)
    print(f&#34;  λ=0 vs λ=0.25 identical bins? {same_025}&#34;)
    print(f&#34;  λ=0.55 peak bin: {peak055}&#34;)
    return curves

rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
n = n_teams * roster_size
ability_beta = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, n, ability_draw=&#34;beta_2_2&#34;,
    ability_mean=0.5, ability_sd=0.15, ability_clip_low=0.0, ability_clip_high=1.0,
    ability_student_t_df=5.0, ability_student_t_scale=1.0)
rng2 = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
ability_z = tpa.draw_abilities(rng2, n, ability_draw=&#34;normal_clipped&#34;,
    ability_mean=0.0, ability_sd=1.0, ability_clip_low=-3.0, ability_clip_high=3.0,

    &#34;viability_theta&#34;: THETA, &#34;viability_sharpness&#34;: GAMMA})

players, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng3, method=&#34;sort_chop&#34;, ability=ability_beta, team_targets=team_targets)

```bash
import tier1_pool_assignment as tpa
import tier1_generative_eda as tge
from sports_pipeline.panel_build import assign_poolq_bin_labels

SEED = 42
n_teams, roster_size, k, n_bins = 350, 16, 560, 16
THETA, GAMMA = 0.72, 10.0

class Sel:
    n_selected = k
    n_bins = n_bins

def run_curve(ability, label):
    n = len(ability)

    params = tpa.AssignmentParams.from_tier1_sim_config()
    params = tpa.AssignmentParams(**{**params.__dict__, "n_teams": n_teams, "roster_size": roster_size,

    med_sd = players.groupby("pool_id")["ability"].std().median()

    curves = {}
    for lam in [0.0, 0.25, 0.55]:
        p = players.copy()
        if lam <= 0:
            out = tpa.assign_selection(p, np.random.default_rng(SEED), n_selected=k,
                score_mode="ability", loo_gap_weight=0.0, winner_selection="C", pool_l_mode="quality",
                viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
        else:
            out = tpa.assign_selection(p, np.random.default_rng(SEED), n_selected=k,
                score_mode="loo_gap_plus_ability", loo_gap_weight=lam, winner_selection="C",
                pool_l_mode="crowding_smooth", viability_theta=THETA, viability_sharpness=GAMMA)
        sel = Sel()
        sel.loo_gap_weight = lam
        sel.score_mode = "loo_gap_plus_ability" if lam > 0 else "ability"
        sel.loo_pool_l_mode = "crowding_smooth" if lam > 0 else "quality"
        summ = tge.inverted_u_bin_table_team_mean(out, sel, assign_poolq_bin_labels=assign_poolq_bin_labels)
        curves[lam] = summ["selection_rate"].to_numpy()
    same_025 = np.allclose(curves[0.0], curves[0.25])
    peak055 = int(curves[0.55].argmax()) + 1
    print(f"{label}: med_team_SD={med_sd:.6f}, unit_interval={on_unit}, l_scale={'OFF' if on_unit else 'ON (~'+str(round(tpa.default_crowding_l_z_scale(ability),2))+')'}")
    print(f"  λ=0 vs λ=0.25 identical bins? {same_025}")
    print(f"  λ=0.55 peak bin: {peak055}")
    return curves

rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
n = n_teams * roster_size
ability_beta = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, n, ability_draw="beta_2_2",
    ability_mean=0.5, ability_sd=0.15, ability_clip_low=0.0, ability_clip_high=1.0,
```

**Short answer: No.** In the sort-and-chop λ diagnostic Alex is looking at, **z-score conversion is not happening** and did **not** create the tiny within-team SD or the rigid λ=0 / λ=0.25 curves. Those come from **sort-and-chop geometry** plus **λ being below the threshold**.

---

## Two different pipelines (easy to mix up)

| Pipeline | Ability scale | Z-scoring? | `l_term_scale` on L_C? |
|----------|---------------|------------|-------------------------|
| **539 sort-chop diagnostic** (your plots) | `beta_2_2` on **[0, 1]** | **No** | **No** — L_C stays on [0,1], same units as A |
| **530 empirical / Alex regressions** | ppm **z-scored within season** | **Yes** (in real data) | **Yes** when generative A is z-ish — multiplies L_C so λ·L can compete with A |

Your λ sweep script uses the **539 track**:

```80:80:sports/scripts/sort_chop_lambda_diagnostic.py
        "ability_draw": str(getattr(mod, "SELECTION_539_ABILITY_DRAW", "beta_2_2")),
```

The code explicitly **skips** z-scaling when A is on [0,1]:

```914:916:sports/tier1_pool_assignment.py
    # Unit-interval A (beta/uniform): L_C ∈ [0,1] is already comparable — no scale.
    if ability_on_unit_interval(ability):
        return l
```

So for Alex’s question on **these** curves: z-scores are a red herring.

---

## Where SD ≈ 0.0002 actually comes from

It is **not** “we z-scored and everything collapsed.” It is **sort-and-chop**:

1. Sort all 5,600 players by \(A_i\).
2. Chop into 350 consecutive blocks of 16.
3. Each team gets **16 adjacent ranks** from the global sorted list.

Neighboring players in the league differ by only ~0.0001 in ability (median gap between adjacent sorted draws). Sixteen of those in a row → **within-team SD ≈ 0.0007** (your plot’s ~0.0002 is the same mechanism; exact number depends on roster size and draw).

That is **built into perfect sort-and-chop**, independent of any z-transform.

Your **zero-overlap experiment** (right panel: set every player’s \(A_i\) = team mean, SD = 0) shows **the same** λ=0 = λ=0.25 curves as the left panel. That is the smoking gun: **even with zero within-team spread, the story is unchanged.** Tiny SD is a symptom of sort-and-chop, not the cause of identical curves.

---

## What *would* z-scoring do (if it were in play)?

Three different things people call “z-scores”:

**1. League-wide z-score of A** (not in this diagnostic)  
- Reorders nobody — same ranks.  
- Would flip on `l_term_scale` (multiply L_C by ~p90−p10 of A).  
- Changes numeric λ calibration, **not** the “A and L_C point the same way” geometry on sort-and-chop.

**2. Within-team z-score of A** (not in code; would be wrong here)  
- Would force each roster to SD ≈ 1 by construction.  
- Would **destroy** the sort-and-chop slice structure. We do **not** do this.

**3. Empirical Alex path: z-score A and L for regression** (538/530 notebooks)  
- For **fitting** \(Y \sim \tilde L + \tilde L^2 + \tilde A\).  
- Separate from generative score \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) in tier1.

The **`l_term_scale` / `CROWDING_L_Z_SCALE`** knob exists so that when A **is** z-scored (530-style `normal_clipped`), congestion isn’t numerically invisible next to A. On **[0,1] beta**, that knob is **off**.

I checked: even with **530 z-ish A** and `l_term_scale` **on**, sort-and-chop still gives **λ=0 vs λ=0.25 identical bins**. So z-scaling doesn’t explain the overlap — the **sort-and-chop A ∥ L_C** structure does.

---

## What actually makes the curves rigid until λ ≈ 0.4

Three stacked facts:

### 1. Between-team overlap = 0  
Sort-and-chop makes **disjoint ability slices**. Team 200’s worst player is still better than team 201’s best. No NCAA-like overlap.

### 2. On these rosters, \(A_i\) and \(L_C\) march together  
- Strong slices (all above θ) → \(L_C \approx\) saturated high  
- Weak slices (all below θ) → \(L_C \approx 0\)  
- One θ-straddle team mixes  

So **Spearman(A, L_C) ≈ 1**. Congestion isn’t a separate axis; it tracks talent.

### 3. Small λ can’t beat that alignment  
Score: \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\).

When high-A players also have high \(L_C\), subtracting \(0.25 \cdot L_C\) is like shaving a proportional tax off everyone — **global order barely moves**. You need \(\lambda \gtrsim 4/\gamma \approx 0.40\) (at γ=10) before congestion at the **θ seams** can flip enough top-K picks to move the 16-bin curve.

That is why:
- **λ=0 and λ=0.25** → same monotone curve (bins 1–14 ≈ 0, only top bins selected)  
- **λ≈0.55+** → hump (peak shifts to bin 11, etc.)

---

## Plain-language answer you can give Alex

*"The identical λ=0 and λ=0.25 curves aren’t from z-scoring. This diagnostic uses Beta ability on [0,1] with no unit rescaling. The tiny within-team SD (~0.0002) comes from sort-and-chop itself — each team is 16 consecutive players from the global ability sort — and we confirmed that even with SD=0 (everyone on a team identical) the curves still match. What matters is that sort-and-chop makes ability and congestion perfectly aligned (high teams are high on both), so small λ doesn’t change who gets selected. The curve only departs once λ crosses about 4/γ (~0.4 at our γ=10); then you get the hump."*

---

## One diagram

```
Sort-and-chop assign
        ↓
Disjoint slices + A ∥ L_C  ← main cause of rigid low-λ curves
        ↓
Small λ: S ≈ A  →  same top-K  →  same 16-bin curve
        ↓
λ > 4/γ: flips at θ seams  →  hump

NOT the cause:
  × z-scoring (off on [0,1] beta)
  × tiny within-team SD alone (zero-overlap panel proves it)
```

Setup used: **40 teams × 15 = 600 players**, **K = 60** (same **K/N = 10%** as gallery), seed 42, same θ=0.72, γ=10.

---

## What changes at N=600

| | N=600, K=60 | N=5600, K=560 |
|--|-------------|---------------|
| Players per bin | ~**38** | ~**350** |
| Median within-team SD | **0.006** (wider slices) | **0.0007** |
| λ=0 vs λ=0.25 | **Not identical** — max \|Δrate\| ≈ **2.7 pp** (bins 15–16) | **Identical** — max \|Δrate\| = **0** |
| Sel flips at λ=0.25 | **10** | **10** |
| Peak bin at λ=0.55 | **Bin 11** (hump) | **Bin 11** (hump) |
| Peak bin at λ=1 | **Bin 9** | **Bin 9** |

So the **story is the same**; the small league is just **noisier**.

---

## What the plot would look like (N=600)

**λ = 0 and λ = 0.25** — still **mostly the same monotone** shape:
- Bins 1–14: all **0**
- Bin 15: **0.61** (λ=0) vs **0.63** (λ=0.25) — tiny visible gap
- Bin 16: **1.00** vs **0.97**

Visually: two lines on top of each other except a small separation at the very top — **not** the full hump yet.

**λ = 0.55** — **hump appears**, same as large N:
- Peak **bin 11** (~0.74)
- Top bin 16 drops to ~**0.08**

**λ = 0.75, 1.0** — peak shifts left (bins 10, 9), same qualitative pattern as gallery.

---

## Is this “rounding”?

**Partially — but only at small N:**

- With ~38 players per bin, rates jump in chunky steps (1/37 ≈ **0.027** — you see exactly **0.0270** in the output). That’s **small-N bin quantization**, not float rounding in the score.
- At N=5600, bins are smooth enough that λ=0.25’s **10 selection flips** don’t move any bin rate — so curves match **exactly**.
- At N=600, those same **10 flips** are enough to nudge bins 15–16 by ~3 pp because each bin has so few teams.

**Bottom line:** The λ=0 = λ=0.25 result at gallery scale is **real physics** (A ∥ L_C, λ below threshold), not a numerical artifact. Shrinking to 600 makes the plot **jaggier** and can show a **small** λ=0 vs λ=0.25 split at the top — but you still don’t get the hump until **λ ≳ 0.55**.

## What happened

Your five λ values were **0.390, 0.395, 0.400, 0.405, 0.410** — all clustered within **±0.01** of λ_crit.

At N=5600 with 16 bins (~350 teams per bin), the **largest bin-rate difference vs λ=0.40** is only:

| δ | λ arms | Max \|Δrate\| vs crit | Visible? |
|---|--------|----------------------|----------|
| **0.005** (yours) | 0.390–0.410 | **0.003** (~0.3 pp) | **No** — lines stack |
| **0.02** (default) | 0.36–0.44 | **0.58** (58 pp at bin 15) | **Yes** |

So your plot is correct: the curves really are identical **in bin space** at that resolution. Selection flips are happening (24–32 players), but they're too few to move any 16-bin rate enough to draw a separate line.

Also: with δ=0.005, even **λ=0.410** doesn't move bins yet. The first visible bin movement at gallery scale is around **λ ≈ 0.42**, not 0.405.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Almost — with one important distinction between “identical selection” and “identical plot.”**

## What “below threshold” means scientifically

On **sort-and-chop**, below **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** (0.40 at γ=10):

- Score \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) **does not reorder enough** to change **who makes global top-K** in any meaningful way.
- So the **selection curve shape** should stay **talent-only monotone**: flat low bins, rise only in the top bins, peak at bin 16.

So yes: **every λ below threshold should give the same qualitative picture** — the same rigid staircase, not a hump.

## Should they be *pixel*-identical?

**At your gallery scale (N=5600, 16 bins): effectively yes.**

| λ (below crit) | Same 16-bin curve as λ=0? | Selection flips vs talent-only |
|----------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 0.25 | **Yes** (exact) | ~10 |
| 0.34, 0.37, 0.40 | **Yes** (max Δ ≈ 0.003 in a bin) | ~16–30 |

So:
- **Individual players** can swap at the cut line (a few dozen out of 5600).
- **16-bin rates** don’t move — too many teams per bin for a handful of flips to show up.

That’s why your below-threshold curves **are** there but **hide under** the thick λ=0.40 line.

## When they would *not* look identical

1. **Smaller N / fewer bins** — e.g. N=600, ~38 teams/bin: you can see small gaps at bins 15–16 even below threshold.
2. **λ = 0 vs λ > 0** — same curve, but score is computed differently (`S=A` vs `S=A−λL_C`); identical *outcome*, not identical *scores*.
3. **Slightly above crit** (0.42+) — curve **starts** to morph; that’s the orange/red lines in your zoom plot.

## One sentence for Alex

> *Below λ_crit, congestion is in the score but too weak to change top-K selection at scale, so every sub-threshold λ should produce the same monotone bin curve as talent-only; the hump only appears once λ clears ~4/γ and enough marginal picks flip.*

**Bottom line:** Same **shape** below threshold — yes, by design. Same **line on the plot** at N=5600 — yes, for practical purposes. Exact **player-by-player** identity — not guaranteed, but those swaps are too rare to move the binned curve.

Here’s what I found and fixed:

## `sort_chop_lambda_threshold_zoom.py` — **crash (fixed)**

**Error:** `NameError: name 'delta' is not defined` in `_arm_style()` (line 189).

`_arm_style` compared `lam` to `crit ± k*delta` but **`delta` was never passed in** — sim arms ran, then the plot step failed.

**Other issues in your edited version:**
- **`lambda_arms`** had grown to **9 arms** (docstring still said 5)
- Legend `elif` chain was **wrong** (e.g. `above_far` would get labeled “above farthest”)
- **`run_arm`** always used `loo_gap_plus_ability`, even for λ ≤ 0 (would break if δ is large)

**Fixes applied:**
- Restored **5 arms:** crit ± 2δ, crit ± δ, crit
- Legend from **arm label**, not fragile `lam` comparisons
- Shared **`_score_config`** with the diagnostic script (λ=0 → talent-only)
- **Auto x-zoom** for 100 bins: default `bin_lo ≈ 85` instead of 10

Both scripts run cleanly now.

---

## `sort_chop_lambda_diagnostic.py` — **no runtime errors**

Runs successfully with the decile grid and 100 bins. Linter warnings are type-checker noise (`ModuleSpec | None`, `plt.Normalize`) — not runtime bugs.

## What you finished (science)

Alex’s puzzle: **why do λ=0 and λ=0.25 look the same on sort-and-chop?**

You answered it (and wrote it up in `06_Lambda_threshold_and_KN_memo.md`):

- Below **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ (~0.4 at γ=10)**, selection barely moves off talent-only; at 16 bins curves can look identical.
- Above λ_crit, the curve **morphs** (hump, peak shifts left).
- **θ × K/N panel** is done — peak bin moves with both knobs (`theta/THETA_KN_sweep_*`).

You said: **no deeper λ threshold work for now.**

Slide **5** in `CHAR_Phase_B_characterization.pptx` is the second **θ** slide — **“Characterize θ — panel with K/N (selectivity)”** (peak-bin heatmap). Slides 4 and 5 share the same **L_C** line in the top-left params box.

## Correct formula (as generated)

\[
L_C \;=\; \mathrm{mean}_{j \neq i}\,\sigma\!\big(\gamma(A_j - \theta)\big)
\]

Read it as:

- **\(j \neq i\)** — leave-one-out over **teammates** on \(i\)’s roster (not the full league; not including self).
- **\(A_j\)** — **peer** ability, not \(A_i\).
- **\(\sigma(x) = 1/(1+e^{-x})\)** — logistic sigmoid (smooth viability), with **\(x = \gamma(A_j - \theta)\)**.
- **\(\theta\)** — viability cutline (the knob on this slide).
- **\(\gamma\)** — sigmoid sharpness (fixed at **10** on this slide).

That matches doc **02** and memo **06**: **`L_C`** = LOO mean of soft peer viability (`crowding_smooth` / `pool_c_smooth_loo` in code).

## What it is *not*

| Wrong | Why |
|--------|-----|
| \(\mathrm{mean}_j\,\sigma(\gamma(A_i - \theta))\) | Uses **own** ability, not peers’ |
| \(\mathrm{mean}_j\, A_j\) | That’s **poolq_loo** / **\(L_Q\)**, not **\(L_C\)** |
| Pool mean (16 players incl. self) | Wrong peer set |
| \(\sigma(\gamma(\theta - A_j))\) | Sign flip on the sigmoid |
| Hard count \(\#\{j \neq i : A_j > \theta\}\) | Hard viability; **539 sim uses smooth** \(\sigma\) |
| \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) in the **\(L_C\)** box | That’s the **score**; this box defines **\(L_C\)** only |

On this slide, **\(\rho=8\)**, **\(\lambda=0.55\)**, **\(\gamma=10\)** are fixed; only **\(\theta\)** and **\(K/N\)** vary. Score is still \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) everywhere in the sim — it’s just not repeated in that top-left equation block.

## If you edited it in PowerPoint

Paste this (Equation Editor or plain text):

```
L_C = mean_{j≠i} σ(γ(A_j − θ))
```

with \(\sigma\) = logistic sigmoid.

Or rerun to restore from source:

```bash
./scripts/build_characterization_slides.sh
```

That overwrites manual edits on the `.pptx` though — if you only fixed slide 5 by hand, copy the line above into that text box.

Good catch — python-pptx rebuilds decks from scratch, so Equation Editor work can't round-trip. Here's the workflow we set up:

## Two-track workflow

| Track | File | Scripts |
|--------|------|---------|
| **Hand (yours)** | `slides/CHAR_Phase_B_characterization.pptx` | **Never overwritten** |
| **Auto (disposable)** | `slides/auto/CHAR_*` and `CHAR_Phase_B_characterization_AUTO.pptx` | Safe to regenerate |

## Commands

**Default — figures only** (what you'll use most days):
```bash
./scripts/build_characterization_slides.sh
```
Updates PNGs/CSVs in `pass_b/`, `pass_c_rho/`, `theta/`, `sort_chop_lambda/`. **No `.pptx` touched.**

**When you want a fresh script-generated template** (compare or copy layout):
```bash
./scripts/build_characterization_slides.sh --auto-slides
```

## When plots change

In your hand deck: **right-click plot → Change Picture** → pick the updated PNG (paths listed in `slides/README.txt`).

Equations and bullets stay as you formatted them; only the image swaps.

## Why not auto-merge equations?

PowerPoint's Equation Editor uses OMML; python-pptx only writes plain/mathtext-ish text. There's no reliable "update figures only, keep OMML" path without PowerPoint automation on your Mac — more fragile than Change Picture for ~7 plots.

---

_**User**_

Hey, real quick, would it make sense to make a surface plot out of slide 5 - maybe as an alternate graphic?  What do you think?

---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — **as an alternate**, but I would **not** replace the current Slide 5 graphic with a surface plot.

## Why it’s tempting

Slide 5 is really “**peak bin** as a function of two knobs” (θ and K/N). That’s naturally a 2D response surface, so a 3D plot can show **interaction**: at low K/N the peak marches up as θ rises; at high K/N everything saturates at bin 16.

## Why I’d be cautious

**You only have a 3×3 grid** (θ ∈ {0.50, 0.72, 0.90} × K/N ∈ {1%, 10%, 40%} → 9 points).

A surface plot would **interpolate** between those points and can imply a smooth θ–K/N law before you’ve committed to one — and PD15 explicitly said **don’t fix θ = f(K/N)** yet.

**Peak bin is discrete** (1…16). Surfacing it suggests false smoothness between, say, bin 6 and bin 9.

**3D on slides** is hard to read in a room, hard to quote exact numbers from, and often prints poorly.

Your current **heatmap / peak-bin panel** (`THETA_KN_sweep_peak_bin.png`) is usually **better for science and for Alex** because you can read the table.

## What I’d do instead

| Option | Verdict |
|--------|--------|
| **Keep heatmap on Slide 5** | Primary — exact, honest for sparse grid |
| **Line plot: peak bin vs θ, one line per K/N** | **Best alternate** — shows interaction, easy to read |
| **Denser grid → then surface/contour** | Good **if** you expand the sweep (e.g. 5 θ × 5 K/N) |
| **3D surface from 3×3 only** | OK as **appendix / exploratory**, weak as main slide |

## Bottom line

**Alternate graphic: yes — line plot or enhanced heatmap.**  
**3D surface from today’s 9 points: only as a secondary “shape intuition” figure**, with a caption like *“3×3 diagnostic grid; lines/surface interpolated — not a fitted θ(K/N) law.”*

If you want, we can add `theta_kn_sweep_diagnostic.py` output for a **line-plot PNG** (and optionally a surface from a denser grid later) under `theta/`, same hand-deck / Change Picture workflow as the other slides.

_**User**_

I put it on slide 5.  DO you think it's alright, or too much?


---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

For **you** reviewing or sending the deck ahead of time, it’s **fine** — not too much. Same 9 cells, two views: the **lines** carry the story (θ matters at 1%, saturates at 40%), the **heatmap** gives exact peak bins without reading off the y-axis.

For **live with Alex**, I’d treat it as **slightly heavy** — not wrong, but you’ll almost always **talk to one graphic** and the other becomes wallpaper.

**Practical split:**

| Use case | Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|
| **Presenting (10 min on Phase B)** | **Line plot only** on slide 5; move heatmap to backup / appendix, or drop it |
| **Deck as reference / email** | **Both OK** — reader can pause and cross-check numbers |
| **One slide in a long deck** | **Both OK** if you don’t dwell — point at green line once, gesture at yellow row once |

**What I’d say out loud if you keep both:**  
“Same 3×3 grid — left is the trend, right is the lookup table. At 1% the peak marches up with θ; at 40% everything’s bin 16.” Then stop; don’t walk every cell.

**If it feels crowded in the room:** drop the heatmap (or shrink it to a small inset). The **line plot alone** is enough for the claim in your footer.

So: **alright for a characterization / working deck**; **trim to one figure** if slide 5 is a punch line in a tight Alex meeting. Your call based on how much time that slide gets.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Great questions — you’re right to tighten the vocabulary. I patched `07_Phase_B_Characterization_Slides_Explained.md` with seed inventory, λ=0.55 provenance, L_C vs λ wording, and sort-and-chop rationale for slides 6–7. Here are the answers in plain language.

---

### 1. What is actually stochastic? (Why seed 42?)

**Random (needs a seed):**
- **Draw abilities** \(A_i\) — Beta(2,2) on [0,1]
- **Draw team targets** \(T_j\) — uniform on [0,1]
- **Soft assignment (ρ slides only)** — shuffle order + weighted random team picks

**Deterministic once rosters exist:**
- **Sort-and-chop** — pure sorting/chopping
- **Score** — compute \(L_C\) from teammates, then \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\)
- **Selection** — winner rule `"C"` = deterministic **top K** by score (what all Phase B scripts use)
- **VISUALIZE** — quantile bins and “fraction selected per bin”

So seed 42 mainly locks **one talent lottery** (\(A_i\), \(T_j\)) per figure family. On ρ slides, each soft-ρ arm also needs its own assignment randomness (with a seed offset) while keeping the **same** abilities.

We are **not** using stochastic selection (`"A"` / `"B"`) in this deck.

---

### 2. Where did λ = 0.55 come from?

**It is the Alex 539 reference preset — not a new Phase B estimate.**

Provenance chain:
- `sports/tier1_539_reference_settings.json` → `"lambda_": 0.55`
- `sports/tier1_sim_config.py` → `SELECTION_539_LOO_GAP_WEIGHT = 0.55`
- Playground default → `tier1_cell10_playground_state.json` → `loo_gap_weight: 0.55`
- Gallery naming → `LAMBDA_MODERATE = 0.55` in `gallery_knobs.py`

**How the deck uses it:**
- **Slides 1–2, 4–5:** λ **fixed** at 0.55 while another knob moves (“run at the 539 reference”)
- **Slide 3:** 0.55 is **one arm** in {0, 0.25, 0.55, 1.0}
- **Slides 6–7:** 0.55 is a **labeled sweep arm**, same preset number

We have **not** claimed 0.55 is the “true” NCAA λ — it is the **benchmark weight** so characterization stays aligned with the 539 playground track.

---

### 3. L_C vs λ — you’re correct

| Symbol | Role |
|--------|------|
| **\(L_C\)** | Congestion **measure** — LOO mean of peer viability σ(γ(A_j − θ)) |
| **λ** | **Weight** on that term in score: \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\) |

**λ is not “the congestion.”** It is how hard congestion **bites in ranking**. The walkthrough slide 3 title was wrong; it now says “weight on **L_C** in score.”

---

### 4. “Congestion belongs in the score, not just the environment story” — what we mean

Yes — your read is right. Three layers:

1. **Environment / hero theory:** \(L_net = B - D\) describes peer effects on development. That is **not** who wins the slot in the sim.
2. **Score (advancement step 1):** We **compute** \(L_C\) from the roster and **subtract** \(\lambda L_C\) in \(S_i\). That **changes ranking**.
3. **VISUALIZE:** Pool-mean bins are **readout** — they show where selected players sit; they do **not** create congestion.

So the sentence means: **\(L_C\) is calculated and used in SCORE**, not merely a plotting choice. Slide 3’s test is λ=0 vs λ>0 with **identical rosters and top-K selection** — only the score formula changes, and curves diverge.

---

### 5. Sigmoid on YouTube

Good plan. In our stack, σ is the **soft step** “does teammate j count as a viable peer?” centered at θ; γ controls steepness. That feeds **\(L_C\)**, which feeds **\(S_i\)**.

---

### 6. Why sort-and-chop on slides 6 and 7? (γ sweep + λ_crit)

**Not** the same reason as slides 1–2 (where ρ is the knob under test).

Slides **6–7** use sort-and-chop as a **controlled testbed**:

1. **Clean geometry** — non-overlapping ability slices; within teams, ability and viability line up → the θ-straddle team and **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** story in memo 06 is visible.
2. **Isolate score reordering** — no soft-assignment noise; the question is *when does λ change who makes top-K?*
3. **Alex’s puzzle** — on sort-and-chop, λ=0.25 can **look** identical to λ=0 because both sit **below λ_crit** for γ=10 (~0.4), so **ranks don’t swap** even though λ appears in the formula.

**Soft ρ=8** = realistic mixing world (slides 1–5). **Sort-and-chop** = extreme benchmark for **viability sharpness (γ)** and **critical λ** — complementary, not contradictory.

---

Re-PDF when ready: `./scripts/convert_single_md_to_pdf.sh 07_Phase_B_Characterization_Slides_Explained.md`

After your sigmoid deep-dive, say the word and we can walk through sort-and-chop again with the θ-straddle picture step by step.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**T_j** is the per-team **talent target** — the ideal “seat” soft assignment tries to fill. Here is the explicit provenance:

### Where T_j comes from

| | |
|---|---|
| **Draw** | `draw_target_means()` in `tier1_pool_assignment.py` |
| **Distribution** | **Uniform**, iid — one independent draw per team |
| **Range (Phase B / 539)** | **[0, 1]** via `SELECTION_539_TARGET_MEAN_LOW/HIGH` in `tier1_sim_config.py` |
| **Seed** | Same lottery as **A_i** — `HERO_SEED = 42` |
| **Real data?** | **No** — synthetic targets, not NCAA school talent or conference strength |

Pass scripts wire this explicitly:

```99:104:sports/scripts/pass_c_rho_ablation_bundle.py
        "target_dist": "uniform",
        "t_low": float(getattr(mod, "SELECTION_539_TARGET_MEAN_LOW", 0.0)),
        "t_high": float(getattr(mod, "SELECTION_539_TARGET_MEAN_HIGH", 1.0)),
```

### What T_j does in the pipeline

- **Soft assignment (ρ slides):** enters the match kernel — teams with **T_j ≈ A_i** get higher weight; ρ controls how sharp that preference is.
- **Sort-and-chop (γ / λ_crit):** **T_j is drawn but unused** — rosters come only from sorting **A_i** and chopping into slices.

The [0,1] band matches **A_i** on [0,1] (Beta(2,2) 539 preset) so both live on the same scale. We have **not** fitted T_j to real rosters in Phase B.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Your YouTube picture is right for **one building block**. In our stack we use it a bit differently from “predict yes/no for the player.” Here is the exact role.

---

## What problem σ is solving

Once rosters exist, we need a number **L_C** = “how congested is *my* peer field?” for the **score**:

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C
\]

Congestion here means: **how many of my teammates count as serious, viable peers** — people good enough that you’re competing with them for attention, minutes, or (in the story) the scarce advancement slot.

The sigmoid is how we turn each teammate’s ability into a **peer-viability score** before averaging.

---

## Step-by-step method (one player *i*)

**Setup:** Player *i* is on a roster. Look at **teammates only** (leave-one-out: exclude *i*).

**Step 1 — For each teammate *j*, compute viability**

\[
v_j = \sigma\big(\gamma(A_j - \theta)\big) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\gamma(A_j - \theta)}}
\]

- **A_j** = teammate *j*’s ability  
- **θ** = viability cutline (“how good does a peer have to be to matter?”)  
- **γ** = sharpness (how binary vs gradual that judgment is)

Interpretation of **v_j**:

| Teammate ability | v_j (roughly) |
|------------------|---------------|
| A_j ≫ θ | ≈ 1 — “fully viable” peer |
| A_j = θ | **exactly 0.5** — on the fence |
| A_j ≪ θ | ≈ 0 — “doesn’t really count as competition” |

So your 0.5 rule applies **per teammate**: at A_j = θ, that peer is half-in, half-out. We do **not** apply a single 0.5 rule to “is player *i* selected?” — selection is **top-K by S_i**.

**Step 2 — Average over teammates (LOO)**

\[
L_C = \mathrm{mean}_{j \neq i}\, v_j = \mathrm{mean}_{j \neq i}\, \sigma(\gamma(A_j - \theta))
\]

- **L_C ≈ 0** — almost no viable peers around you  
- **L_C ≈ 1** — almost every teammate is a viable peer → **high congestion**

**Step 3 — Enter score**

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C
\]

High **L_C** **lowers** your score even if **A_i** is high — “talented, but buried among other viable players.”

**Step 4 — Select**  
Top **K** by **S_i** (deterministic in Phase B). Bins on the slides are just **readout** of where those selected players sit on pool mean.

That’s the full chain: **σ on each peer → average → subtract in score → rank → select.**

---

## Concrete mini-example

θ = 0.72, γ = 10, λ = 0.55. You have 3 teammates with abilities 0.90, 0.75, 0.50:

- j=1: A=0.90 → σ large (~0.85+) — viable  
- j=2: A=0.75 → σ ≈ 0.5+ — borderline viable  
- j=3: A=0.50 → σ small (~0.1) — not really viable  

**L_C** = mean of those three ≈ **0.5** (moderate congestion).  
If **A_i = 0.80**: **S_i ≈ 0.80 − 0.55×0.5 = 0.525**.

Same talent on a weak team (teammates all ~0.40) → **L_C ≈ 0** → **S_i ≈ 0.80**. Same **A_i**, different roster context → different rank.

---

## Why a sigmoid (and not just “count peers above θ”)?

The code actually has **both**:

```774:775:sports/tier1_pool_assignment.py
      pool_c_loo          — L_C hard: share of teammates with ability > θ  ∈ [0,1]
      pool_c_smooth_loo   — L_C soft: mean teammate σ(γ(A−θ))              ∈ [0,1]
```

**Phase B / Alex 539 track uses the smooth one** (`crowding_smooth`).

Reasons:

1. **Story:** “Viable peer” is not literally on/off — a teammate slightly above θ matters more than one far below. σ gives a **graded** contribution.
2. **Knobs:** **θ** moves the center of the step; **γ** moves from “fuzzy” to “almost hard threshold.” That’s what your θ and γ slides characterize.
3. **Math:** Smooth σ avoids a cliff at θ; λ_crit and sort-and-chop algebra use the logistic knee (memo 06: λ_crit ≈ 4/γ).

Hard version (count share with A_j > θ) is the limit γ → ∞ in spirit. We keep smooth σ as the default.

---

## What σ is *not* doing here

| You might think… | Actually… |
|------------------|-----------|
| σ decides if *i* gets drafted | No — **top-K on S_i** decides |
| σ outputs a draft probability for *i* | No — it scores **each teammate’s viability**, then we **average** |
| We always binarize at 0.5 | No — we **average** soft values; 0.5 is only the value **at A_j = θ** |
| σ is assignment (ρ) | No — assignment is separate (match to **T_j**) |
| σ is the hero curve | No — hero is **real outcomes**; σ is inside **fake-league score** |

---

## Why this design (dissertation logic)

**Layer B story:** Good peers can help (B) and hurt (D/congestion). **L_C** is the **D-ish congestion measure on the roster** after assignment — “how crowded is my viable-peer field?”

**Layer C (sim):** We need that idea **inside advancement**, not only in prose. So:

- Assignment (ρ) puts you on a roster  
- **σ + θ + γ** define who counts as a viable peer on that roster  
- **L_C** summarizes peer congestion  
- **λ** weights it in **score**  
- **Top-K** picks winners  

The **knockout** on slide 3: same rosters, **λ = 0** vs **λ > 0**. Only difference is whether **L_C** (built with σ) enters **S_i**. That tests “congestion in score matters,” not “sigmoid predicts draft.”

---

## One sentence to keep

**σ turns each teammate’s ability into “how much does this peer count as viable competition?”; L_C averages that over your teammates; λ subtracts that average from your talent in the ranking.**

When you’re ready on sort-and-chop, the θ-straddle team story in memo 06 is exactly “where on the roster σ flips from ≈0 to ≈1 and λ first changes who makes top-K.”

Good — three related but distinct points. Here is the clean version, plus what we added to the deck docs.

---

## 1. Hard vs smooth L_C (documented in slides + walkthrough)

The code builds **both** in `add_loo_pool_columns()`:

| Mode | Config | Per-teammate *j* | **L_C** for player *i* |
|------|--------|------------------|------------------------|
| **Smooth (Phase B deck)** | `crowding_smooth` | σ(γ(A_j − θ)) | LOO **mean** of those weights |
| **Hard (in code, not in deck)** | `crowding` | 1 if A_j > θ else 0 | LOO **share** above θ |

**This deck uses smooth only** (`loo_pool_l_mode="crowding_smooth"` everywhere in Pass B/C and θ/γ diagnostics).

**Updated:**
- Intro slide — **L_C** glossary row + bullet in “How to read this deck”
- Walkthrough — new section **“Hard vs smooth L_C”**
- θ slide auto-builder — `$L_C$ mode: crowding_smooth` note
- Optional figure: `sort_chop_lambda/VIABILITY_hard_vs_smooth.png` (now in `./scripts/build_characterization_slides.sh`)

---

## 2. What would you see with hard L_C?

**Same big story** — λ in score still bends who gets selected. **Different mechanics:**

| | Smooth (what we show) | Hard (counterfactual) |
|---|----------------------|------------------------|
| **γ** | **Matters** — γ sweep slides make sense | **Irrelevant** — only θ; γ sweep would be pointless |
| **Peers near θ** | Graded (~0.5 at A_j = θ) | **Cliff** at θ |
| **L_C values** | Continuous in [0,1] | **Discrete** (0, 1/15, 2/15, …) |
| **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** | Holds on sort-and-chop (memo 06) | No — sharper cliff; reorder tied to **θ** only |
| **Curve shapes** | Humps, softer transitions | Often **sharper**; same qualitative “congestion bends selection” |

**One-liner if Alex asks:** “Smooth σ is the graded peer-viability story and lets γ be a knob; hard share is the binary limit (γ → ∞). Phase B standardizes on smooth so θ and γ slides hang together.”

The hard-vs-smooth figure shows a θ-straddle roster: soft **L_C ≈ 0.52** vs hard **L_C = 0.43** for the same teammates — same *kind* of interior congestion, different numbers and no γ in the hard case.

---

## 3. Sort-and-chop — your read is basically right

**Yes:** sort-and-chop is **maximum assignment assortativity** — it **removes ambiguity in roster geometry** so γ and λ_crit are easier to characterize.

More precisely:

- **Soft ρ (slides 1–5):** realistic mixing; team talent windows **overlap** (~99% of team pairs overlap on the ability axis). Good for “does assignment matter?” — noisy for “where exactly does λ first reorder ranks?”
- **Sort-and-chop (slides 6–7):** sort all players by **A_i**, chop into equal rosters → **zero between-team overlap**. One **θ-straddle** team, clean **seams** at slice boundaries → λ_crit ≈ 4/γ story is visible.

**Important distinction:** Sort-and-chop is **not** the ρ knob. It **ignores T_j** and is a **hard diagnostic benchmark** (“perfect rank sorting”), not “NCAA-realistic seating.”

**Pairing in the deck:**
- ρ slides → **realistic** assignment world  
- γ / λ_crit slides → **controlled testbed** with extreme, deterministic roster geometry  

Same score rule (**smooth L_C**); different assignment extreme.

---

**Implementation sketch:** In `add_loo_pool_columns` / score path, add something like `pool_c_team` = mean σ(γ(A_j − θ)) over **all** roster members (or all teammates, no LOO). Score uses that team value for every player on team *j*.

**Env flag example:** `GALLERY_LC_MODE=team` vs default `loo_smooth` — so `./scripts/build_characterization_slides.sh` still produces **today’s PNGs** unless you opt in.

### Part B — **θ(K/N)** (naive-draft quantile)

| Today | PD16 direction |
|-------|----------------|
| **θ = 0.72** fixed (539 preset) | **θ = quantile** of the ability draw: find **A\*** so **P(A > A\*) = K/N** |
| Same θ at 1%, 10%, 40% selectivity in θ×K/N grid | θ **moves with K/N** by construction (your whiteboard Beta tail sketch) |

For Beta(2,2) on [0,1]: θ = `beta.ppf(1 - K/N, 2, 2)`. At K/N = 10%, that’s roughly **0.68**, not 0.72 — numbers will shift slightly.

**Env flag example:** `GALLERY_THETA_MODE=k_over_n` vs `preset` (0.72).

### “Compare to current deck numbers”

After flipping flags, **re-run the same diagnostics** (Pass B λ, θ OAT, θ×K/N, etc.) and ask:

- Do curves still **bend** the same way qualitatively?
- How much do peak bins / λ_crit-style readouts **move** numerically?
- Does θ×K/N grid **change character** when θ is tied to K/N (Alex expects interpretation to solidify; some grid cells may collapse or shift)?

Goal: **evidence for Alex** — “PD16 changes are small / large / wrong direction” — before you replace benchmark text on the intro slide or re-brief.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Yes — you can close that editor tab without saving.** That's the right move.

## What SpecStory actually does

**Save AI Chat History** does two things:

1. **Writes the archive** to `.specstory/history/` (timestamped files like `2026-06-11_08-19-11-0400-compass.md`).
2. **Opens a preview** in a new editor tab so you can read the export.

The tab in the editor is a **preview**, not something you need to Save As elsewhere.

## If you click "Don't save" on the unusual line terminators warning

That's fine. SpecStory exports sometimes include Unicode line separators (U+2028 / U+2029). Cursor flags them; they're harmless for the archive.

- **Don't save the preview tab** → nothing extra is written; the copy in `.specstory/history/` is what counts.
- **Do save the preview tab** somewhere like `sports/documents/` → you get a **duplicate** (that's how files like `<!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.md` ended up in the repo before).

**Workflow:** Run save → select conversations → OK → **close the preview tab** (Cmd+W). Don't Save is correct.

## Where the history actually lives

```
.specstory/history/
  2026-06-11_08-19-11-0400-compass.md   ← main ongoing archive (updated today)
  2026-05-24_12-52-09-0400-scout.md
  ...
```

That's what git tracks (per your commit rules) and what auto-save updates. To **read** old chats, open files there — not the Untitled preview.

**Quick check after a save:** look in `.specstory/history/` for a file whose timestamp just updated. If it's there, you're done regardless of what you did with the preview tab.

Done. Here is what changed:

## Archived

- **`CHARLES_CHECKLIST_archive_20260804_pd15.md`** — frozen copy of the PD15 checklist (Phase A gallery → Phase B OAT deck). Header explains why it was superseded after PD16.

## New live checklist

**[`CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md`](3-Master_Plan/re_entry/CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md)** — post-PD16 structure:

1. **Locked artifacts** — deck, walkthrough (07), PD16 doc (08), PNGs, scripts (no redo unless asked)
2. **Phase B sign-off** — deck is *built*; you mark `[x]` as you approve each slide’s claim (A_i / t_j still not built)
3. **PD16 follow-ups (priority order)** — team L_C → θ(K/N) → L_C-vs-ρ figures → ρ→0.001 + intuition → intro/doc update → env-var walkthrough
4. **Lingering from PD15** — Phase A `So_Far_.pptx` gallery items (still all `[ ]`, lower priority)
5. **Phase C** — calibration roadmap (ρ, θ, γ, λ from data; PD14 magnitude; notation cleanup)

## Pointers updated

- **`PARKED_FOR_LATER.md`** — both checklist archives + PD15 notes parked as context (near-term = PD16)
- **`00_READ_ME_FIRST.md`** — doc **08** in reading table; checklist section now says post-PD16
- **`transcripts/PD16_notes.md`** — links to live checklist; checklist refresh marked done

## Your next moves (from the checklist)

1. Sign off slides in **`CHAR_Phase_B_characterization.pptx`** (mark Phase B rows as you approve)
2. Start **team-level L_C** when you are ready to implement (`GALLERY_LC_MODE`)
3. **Phase A gallery** can wait unless Alex asks for `So_Far_.pptx` first

If you want doc **08** PDF refreshed after this, run your usual convert script on the updated paths — I did not regenerate PDFs.

No — there isn’t a separate checklist archive folder today, and that’s intentional.

**Current convention:** superseded checklists stay **in place** under `3-Master_Plan/re_entry/` with dated names:

- `CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md` — live
- `CHARLES_CHECKLIST_archive_20260804_pd15.md`
- `CHARLES_CHECKLIST_archive_20260803.md`

That matches how re-entry was set up: [`PARKED_FOR_LATER.md`](3-Master_Plan/re_entry/PARKED_FOR_LATER.md) says these are **“archived in place”** so you don’t have to hunt another tree. Pointers live in `00_READ_ME_FIRST.md`, the live checklist, and `PARKED_FOR_LATER.md`.

**Other “archive” locations in the repo serve different jobs:**

| Folder | Use |
|--------|-----|
| `3-Master_Plan/obsolete/` | Old agent mail, superseded COMPASS docs — not Charles checklists |
| `sports/archive/` | Retired notebooks |
| `re_entry/HEROs_and_PASSes/.../archive/` | Old sweep CSVs / experiments |

So for checklists, **archive-in-place + `_archive_YYYYMMDD` suffix** is the appropriate pattern, not a subfolder.

If you want a tidier `re_entry/` root, a reasonable addition would be `re_entry/archive/checklists/` with a one-line `README.txt` — but we’d need to **move the two archive files and update links** in `00`, `PARKED`, `CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md`, and `PD15_notes.md`. Worth doing only if clutter bothers you; functionally the current setup is correct.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Model change #2** is Alex’s way of saying: stop picking θ by hand (like 0.72 from the 539 preset). **Derive it from how selective the league is (K/N) and what the ability distribution looks like.**

---

## The shorthand decoded

**θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N)**

Read it in three pieces:

| Piece | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **A** | Player ability (what you draw as **A_i** — Beta(2,2) on [0,1] in the sim, or empirical talent in data) |
| **F_A** | **CDF** of ability: F_A(a) = P(A ≤ a) = “fraction of players at or below ability *a*” |
| **F_A⁻¹** | **Inverse CDF** (quantile function): “what ability level has exactly fraction *p* of the population at or below it?” |
| **K/N** | Selection rate — e.g. K=560 slots, N=5600 players → **10%** advance |
| **1 − K/N** | Fraction that **does not** advance (if K/N advance, then 1−K/N stay below the cutoff) |

So:

**θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N)** means:

> Find the ability cutoff where **(1 − K/N)** of players are at or below it — equivalently, **K/N** of players are above it.

That cutoff **is** θ.

---

## Plain-English version (Alex’s “naive draft”)

1. Imagine **no teams**, no congestion, no sigmoid ambiguity — pure talent ranking.
2. Exactly **K/N** of the league gets drafted (top K out of N).
3. Draw the ability curve (PDF). Find cutoff **A\*** so the **area to the right** equals **K/N**:

```text
P(A > A*) = K/N
```

4. Set **θ = A\***.

The sigmoid σ(γ(A_j − θ)) then adds **soft ambiguity around that cliff**, not the cliff itself.

---

## Why “CDF” shows up

The CDF is just the bookkeeping for “what fraction is below this point?”

- **F_A(θ) = P(A ≤ θ) = 1 − K/N**
- Solve for θ → **θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N)**

Same idea as: “θ is the **(1−K/N) quantile** of the ability distribution” — e.g. at K/N = 10%, θ is the **90th percentile** of A.

---

## Concrete example (sim default)

Ability draw: **Beta(2,2)** on [0,1].  
K/N = **10%** → 1 − K/N = **0.90**.

In Python:

```python
from scipy.stats import beta
theta = beta.ppf(1 - K/N, 2, 2)   # ≈ 0.68 at 10%
```

Compare to today’s preset **θ = 0.72** — close, but **not tied to K/N**. If K/N = 1% (MBB-like), the quantile θ drops; at 40% (Army-like), it rises. That’s why the θ×K/N grid used fixed {0.50, 0.72, 0.90} before PD16; after PD16, θ **tracks K/N by construction** when `GALLERY_THETA_MODE=k_over_n`.

---

## One-line summary

**θ is the talent level that separates the top K/N of the ability distribution from the rest** — computed from the CDF/quantile, not chosen as a free knob.

If helpful, I can add this decode as a short box in doc **08** or the PD16 notes so you don’t have to re-derive F_A⁻¹ each time.

_**User**_

What would that formula look like hand written or in Latex

---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

## LaTeX

**Cutoff definition (Alex’s whiteboard):**

\[
\mathbb{P}(A_i > \theta) = \frac{K}{N}
\]

**Equivalent CDF form:**

\[
F_A(\theta) = \mathbb{P}(A_i \le \theta) = 1 - \frac{K}{N}
\]

**Quantile / inverse-CDF (the PD16 shorthand):**

\[
\boxed{\theta = F_A^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{K}{N}\right)}
\]

**With the sigmoid layered on top (what the model actually uses):**

\[
\sigma\!\bigl(\gamma\,(A_j - \theta)\bigr), \qquad \theta = F_A^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{K}{N}\right)
\]

**Beta(2,2) sim example:**

\[
\theta = F_{\mathrm{Beta}(2,2)}^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{K}{N}\right)
\]

In code that’s `scipy.stats.beta.ppf(1 - K/N, 2, 2)`.

---

## Handwritten-style (what Alex was drawing)

```text
        f(A)  ▲
              │     ╱╲
              │    ╱  ╲
              │   ╱    ╲____
              │  ╱│←───→│
              └──┴───A*──┴────► A
                  θ = A*

   area to the RIGHT of θ  =  K/N
   area to the LEFT  of θ  =  1 − K/N
```

Or as a one-liner on the margin:

```text
   θ  :=  the ability where  P(A > θ) = K/N
        =  F_A^{-1}(1 − K/N)
```

---

## Copy-paste LaTeX block (for a slide or memo)

```latex
% Naive-draft viability threshold (PD16)
\mathbb{P}(A_i > \theta) = \frac{K}{N}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
F_A(\theta) = 1 - \frac{K}{N}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\theta = F_A^{-1}\!\left(1 - \frac{K}{N}\right)
```

The middle step is the CDF; the last line is the inverse-CDF / quantile shorthand from the PD16 notes.

## Comment strategy (my proposal — approve before we code)

### Principle: three layers, not wall-of-text

Your codebase already has good module-level glossaries in `tier1_pool_assignment.py`. PD16 comments should **extend that pattern**, not duplicate doc 07/08 in every function.

| Layer | Where | Purpose | Length |
|-------|--------|---------|--------|
| **A. PD16 banner** | Top of `gallery_knobs.py` + one block in `tier1_pool_assignment.py` | *Why* Aug 2026 changed L_C and θ; pointer to doc 08 | ~15–25 lines once |
| **B. Mode dispatch** | Functions that branch on `LC_MODE` / `THETA_MODE` | *What differs* between `loo_smooth` vs `team_smooth`, `preset` vs `k_over_n` | 3–5 lines per branch |
| **C. Line math** | Inside team-L_C and theta-quantile helpers only | *How* the formula is implemented (LOO subtract self vs team mean; `ppf(1−K/N)`) | 1 line where non-obvious |

**Avoid:** repeating the full naive-draft story in every diagnostic script. Those scripts get **one import-line comment** + footer text on the PNG title, not another essay.

---

### What each file should say (concrete)

**1. `gallery_knobs.py`** — the “control panel” comment block:

```python
# PD16 modes (Paper Directions 16, Aug 2026 — see re_entry/08_PD16_…)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# GALLERY_LC_MODE:
#   loo_smooth  — DEFAULT. L_C = LOO mean σ(γ(A−θ)); current Phase B deck.
#   team_smooth — PD16. L_C = team-level mean σ(γ(A−θ)); same for all roster.
#
# GALLERY_THETA_MODE:
#   preset      — DEFAULT. θ from tier1_539_reference_settings (0.72).
#   k_over_n    — PD16. θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N); naive-draft quantile on ability draw.
#
# Output variant: set GALLERY_OUTPUT_SUFFIX=_pd16 (or per-pass *_PNG_SUFFIX)
# so baseline PNGs are never overwritten — compare old vs new in hand deck.
```

That’s the comment **you** read when exporting env vars six months from now.

**2. `tier1_pool_assignment.py`** — one new section header + focused docstrings:

```python
# =============================================================================
# 5b. TEAM-LEVEL L_C (PD16) — same σ(γ(A−θ)), no leave-one-out
# =============================================================================
# Alex PD16: congestion is a property of team j, not “my LOO teammates.”
# Writes pool_c_smooth_team (broadcast to every player on pool_id).
# Score path still uses the same column resolver — only the L column name changes.
```

Inside `add_team_crowding_columns()`:

```python
# Team smooth L_C: mean_j σ(γ(A_k − θ)) over ALL k on roster (include self).
# Unlike add_loo_pool_columns, we do NOT subtract player i — same L_C for whole team.
```

**3. `resolve_viability_theta()` (new helper in gallery_knobs or pool_assignment)**:

```python
def resolve_viability_theta(...) -> float:
    """Return θ for L_C and sigmoid.

    preset:   fixed 539 value (Phase B deck baseline).
    k_over_n: θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N) — top K/N tail of ability draw (PD16 naive draft).
              Beta(2,2) in sim: scipy.stats.beta.ppf(1 - k_over_n, 2, 2).
    """
```

**4. Diagnostic scripts** (`pass_c_rho_ablation_bundle.py`, etc.) — minimal:

```python
# Reads LC_MODE / THETA_MODE from gallery_knobs; writes *{GALLERY_OUTPUT_SUFFIX}.png
```

**5. Slide builders** — title/footer strings, not code comments:

PNG subtitle line like: `PD16: team L_C, θ=0.68 (K/N quantile)` so the **figure** carries the provenance when old/new sit back-to-back.

```bash
export GALLERY_THETA_MODE=k_over_n
```

Short answer: **No.** Alex did **not** say to compute ρ the same way as θ (no CDF quantile, no “ρ = F⁻¹(1 − K/N)” formula).

---

## What Alex said about ρ (three different things)

### 1. **Interpretation** (immediate — whiteboard Sketch A)

ρ **dials how spread out team L_C is** across the league:

- **Low ρ** → narrow spike (teams look similar in congestion)
- **High ρ** → spread / bimodal (weak teams L_C ≈ 0, strong teams high L_C)

That’s a **story about what ρ does inside the model**, not a formula for picking ρ from data.

**New work:** histogram of # teams vs L_C per ρ arm + 2D heatmap (team ability vs L_C).

### 2. **Characterization tweak** (still OAT, not calibration)

- Low-ρ arm still not flat enough → try **ρ → 0.001**
- One clean **intuition sentence** for why ρ matters in *this* construction

That’s still sensitivity slides, not “derive ρ from a CDF.”

### 3. **Calibration** (later — Phase C)

From the end-of-meeting roadmap:

| Knob | How to pin it |
|------|----------------|
| **θ** | **Quantile:** θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N) — **closed form** from ability draw + selectivity |
| **ρ** | **Match assignment assortativity in data** — empirical fit to how teams/rosters sort in the panel |

So ρ is **data-identified**, like θ, but **not via the same mechanism**. θ comes from a **naive-draft tail cut** on the ability distribution. ρ comes from **matching how assignment works in the data** (assortativity of team formation / roster sorting).

---

## Side-by-side

| | **θ (PD16)** | **ρ (PD16)** |
|---|--------------|--------------|
| **Principled definition?** | Yes — naive draft cutoff | Yes — but **different object** |
| **Formula given?** | P(A > θ) = K/N → θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N) | **No** quantile formula |
| **From what?** | Ability distribution + K/N | **Assignment** assortativity in empirical data |
| **Immediate coding ask** | Implement `k_over_n` theta mode | Team L_C + **L_C-vs-ρ diagnostic** figures |
| **Still a sweep knob?** | Yes, until k_over_n mode lands | **Yes** — OAT ρ arms stay; calibration is later |

---

## Quote to keep in mind

> “Assortativity is this dialing measure of what’s the spread of the L_Cs.”

That’s **interpretation + diagnostic**, not “compute ρ like θ.”

---

## Implication for your `_pd16` work

**In scope now:** team L_C + θ(K/N) → `_pd16` PNGs for ρ/λ/θ slides (same ρ **sweep arms**, new L_C and θ machinery underneath).

**Separate track (ρ):** new **L_C distribution vs ρ** figures (Sketch A) — that’s the ρ-specific PD16 deliverable Alex actually asked for, not a ρ-from-CDF helper.

When you’re ready to implement, we can keep ρ arms as `{0.1, 1, 8, 32}` (plus maybe 0.001) and only change what L_C and θ mean under the hood for the `_pd16` variants.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — **eventually** Alex wants ρ **data-linked**, but **not** like θ. That’s the main thing to keep straight.

---

## What Alex actually said about ρ

Three layers, easy to merge by accident:

| Layer | What | Like θ? |
|-------|------|---------|
| **Now (PD16)** | New **diagnostic**: as ρ sweeps, show how **team L_C spreads** (histogram + heatmap) | No — still OAT, ρ = {0.1, 1, 8, …} |
| **Interpretation** | ρ **dials spread of L_C across teams** | No — story about the mechanism |
| **Later (calibration)** | **“Match assignment assortativity in data”** | **Partially** — data-identified, but **no CDF formula** |

θ: closed form — θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N).

ρ: “find the ρ in our **assignment rule** that matches how sorted / overlapping rosters look in **this domain’s panel**.” Estimator **TBD**; not given at PD16.

---

## Yes, you need ρ to **build assignments**

In the sim pipeline:

```text
draw A_i, T_j  →  soft_assign(ρ)  →  rosters  →  compute L_C  →  score  →  select top K
```

ρ lives in **assignment** (who plays with whom), not in the score. Without it you only have sort-and-chop (ρ → ∞ benchmark) or random mixing (ρ → 0).

For **Phase B / `_pd16` work**, you still **pick ρ arms** for sensitivity — same as today. Alex is **not** asking you to estimate ρ from MBB data before generating `_pd16` PNGs.

---

## “Look at empirical data to get ρ?” — what that would mean

**Yes, in Phase C** — per domain, something like:

- How tightly does player ability align with team quality / target **T_j**?
- How much do talent distributions **overlap** across teams vs sort into tiers?
- If you fit the soft-assign kernel exp(−ρ(A−T)²/…), what ρ reproduces observed roster sorting?

That uses **roster / assignment structure** in the panel (530 for MBB, Army unit data, etc.) — **not** the hero curve, and **not** draft outcomes directly.

Doc 02 already says: *“Calibrating ρ to 530 … is **not** the v1 gate”* — parked under Phase C in your checklist.

---

## How that fits a **general cross-domain model**

The dissertation claim is **structural generality**, not **one global number for every knob**.

| Input | Domain-specific? | How it generalizes |
|-------|------------------|--------------------|
| **K/N** | Yes | MBB ~1%, Army ~40%, gallery 10% |
| **A_i distribution** | Yes | Empirical perf or declared draw (Beta in sim) |
| **θ** | Yes (PD16) | **Same rule everywhere:** quantile at 1−K/N on **that domain’s** A distribution |
| **ρ** | Yes | **Same assignment mechanism everywhere:** soft match to T_j — but **ρ̂ differs** by how sorted that domain’s rosters are |
| **γ, λ** | TBD | Structural constants vs domain-specific — still open |

**Analogy:** a gravity model has the same equation everywhere; **G** doesn’t — you calibrate to local data. Here:

- **Same pipeline:** ASSIGN(ρ) → SCORE(λ, L_C) → SELECT(K)
- **Different calibrated inputs** per domain: K/N, A distribution, ρ̂, (later γ̂, λ̂)

θ generalizes via a **rule** (naive-draft quantile).  
ρ generalizes via a **mechanism** (assortative assignment) + **domain-specific fit** (match empirical sorting).

You do **not** need one ρ = 8.0 for Army, MBB, and tenure. You need: *“In each domain, we measure roster assortativity and set ρ accordingly; the L_C-spread story should line up with the diagnostic.”*

---

## What this means for your next coding step

**Do now (`_pd16`):**

- Team L_C + θ(K/N)
- Regenerate ρ/λ/θ slides with `_pd16` suffix (ρ arms unchanged)
- **New** L_C-vs-ρ diagnostic figures (Sketch A)

**Do not block on:**

- Estimating ρ from 530
- Resolving cross-domain ρ in one shot

**Do later (Phase C):**

- Define ρ̂ for MBB (530 rosters)
- Repeat for Army / tenure when those panels are ready
- Check: does calibrated ρ plus team L_C reproduce the **kind** of L_C spread Alex drew?

---

## One sentence to carry

**θ** = same **formula**, different inputs (A, K/N).  
**ρ** = same **assignment rule**, different **fitted strength** per domain from how teams actually sort talent.

If you want, next we can sketch what a minimal ρ̂ from 530 might look like (even as a one-paragraph “Phase C stub”) so Phase C doesn’t feel like a blank — but it shouldn’t gate the `_pd16` implementation.

---

Good slides — the comparisons tell a coherent story, and nothing looks like a broken pipeline.

## Overall read

**PD16 changes the magnitudes and where peaks land, but not the qualitative claims Phase B was making.** Assignment (ρ) and congestion-in-score (λ) still move the curves the way Alex wanted. Team L_C + θ = F_A⁻¹(1−K/N) mainly **sharpens** those stories at the top bins rather than reversing them.

One caveat: both knobs changed together in `_pd16`, so you cannot yet say “team L_C alone did X.” For Alex, that is probably fine for now — this is “before/after PD16 definition,” not full ablation.

---

## ρ (Pass C) — assortativity still matters, more at the top

| What you see | Interpretation |
|--------------|----------------|
| **ρ = 0.1, 1.0** — noisy, flat-ish, similar before/after | Low mixing still does not produce a strong inverted-U on pool mean. Same message as before. |
| **ρ = 8, 32** — climb starts later; **purple peaks higher** (~0.25 vs ~0.22) and later (bin 14) | High assortativity **bites harder** under team L_C + θ ≈ 0.804. Elite-bin separation between low-ρ and high-ρ is **clearer** in PD16. |
| Low bins still near zero for high ρ | Sort-and-chop-style “weak teams don’t advance” story still there. |

**For Alex:** ρ still dials how much assignment sorting shows up in selection — and with team L_C, the high-ρ arms are **more dramatic** at the top, which fits his “ρ spreads team L_C across the league” intuition (even before you build the histogram diagnostic).

---

## λ (Pass B) — congestion-in-score still bends; λ=0 unchanged = sanity check

| What you see | Interpretation |
|--------------|----------------|
| **λ = 0** (blue) — nearly identical | Correct: no L_C in score → team vs LOO L_C should not matter. Good implementation check. |
| **λ = 0.55** — peak slightly **higher** (~0.19 vs ~0.18) at bin 13 | Baseline congestion arm a bit stronger under PD16 definitions. |
| **λ = 1** — peak shifts from bin **8 → ~10–11**; elite drop still there but later | High λ still compresses/kills the top, but team-level congestion may **delay** where the penalty hits — worth one sentence on the slide footer. |

**For Alex:** Pass A/B knockout logic still holds: λ in the score bends who gets selected; talent-only is monotone.

---

## θ OAT — computed θ is not “just 0.72 with extra steps”

The single **θ = 0.804** curve sits **between** your old 0.72 and 0.90 arms — exactly where a higher, K/N-linked cutline should land.

- Steeper than 0.72, less extreme than 0.90  
- Peak ~bin 13 at ~0.195  

**For Alex:** Preset 0.72 was a reasonable teaching default, but **naive-draft θ at K/N = 10%** is more selective and moves the curve. That supports PD16’s “θ from ability + K/N,” not “keep 0.72 forever.”

---

## θ × K/N — the co-movement story is now built in

| K/N | Computed θ | Peak bin (PD16) |
|-----|------------|-----------------|
| 1% (MBB-like) | ~0.94 | 12 |
| 10% | ~0.80 | 13 |
| 40% | ~0.57 | 16 |

Peak bin **rises with selectivity** when θ tracks K/N — that is the PD16 design working. At 40% K/N you still saturate at bin 16 (everyone-advances-ish regime).

Compared to the old 3×3 grid at “similar θ”: not point-for-point identical (expected — θ is **defined** by K/N now, not free), but the **pattern** is sensible: tighter selection + higher θ at low K/N; looser θ + higher K/N at Army-like rates.

---

## What I would say to Alex in one breath

> “We kept the same assign → score → select pipeline. PD16 only changes **how L_C is measured** (team vs LOO) and **how θ is set** (K/N quantile vs 0.72 preset). The ρ and λ characterization stories still hold; high-ρ and high-λ effects are **stronger at elite bins**. θ = F_A⁻¹(1−K/N) sits between our old OAT arms and co-moves with K/N as intended. Next: L_C-vs-ρ histograms to give ρ a model-internal interpretation.”

---

1. **ρ slide:** “PD16: high ρ peaks later/higher — assortativity + team congestion.”  
2. **λ slide:** “λ = 0 unchanged → confirms toggle; λ > 0 bend shifts with team L_C.”  
3. **θ slide:** “θ = 0.804 = Beta(2,2) quantile at K/N = 10%; not comparable to θ OAT grid — different experiment.”  
4. **θ×K/N:** Label the three points with (K/N, θ) pairs so Alex sees θ tracking explicitly.

If you want to go one level deeper before the next meeting, a useful follow-up run would be **ablation PNGs**: `team_smooth` + preset θ, and `loo_smooth` + k_over_n θ — two suffixes, four combinations. Yes. Every `_pd16` plot changes **both** things at once:

| | **Baseline (left / old)** | **PD16 (right / `_pd16`)** |
|---|---------------------------|----------------------------|
| **L_C** | LOO — mean σ(γ(A−θ)) over **teammates excluding you** (`pool_c_smooth_loo`) | **Team** — same formula over the **full roster**, same value for everyone on the team (`pool_c_smooth_team`) |
| **θ** | Preset **0.72** (539) | **Computed** θ = F_A⁻¹(1 − K/N) — at K/N = 10% that is **≈ 0.804** on Beta(2,2) |

So when you say “before vs after θ standardization,” the slides are really **before vs after the full PD16 package**: **team L_C + naive-draft θ**.

That matches why:
- **λ = 0** barely moves (no L_C in the score — team vs LOO almost irrelevant there)
- **λ > 0** and **ρ** arms **do** move (L_C is in the score and depends on roster structure)

You **cannot** read the comparison and say “this wiggle is only team L_C” or “only θ” without extra runs.

**Settings:** team L_C, θ ≈ 0.804 (naive draft at K/N=10%), same league draw (seed 42), ρ arms: 0.001, 0.1, 1, 8, 32.

## Story for Alex (matches his whiteboard)

**1D — ρ spreads team congestion**
- **Low ρ (0.001–1):** one narrow hump around L_C ≈ 0.15 — teams look alike.
- **High ρ (8):** bimodal — pile at L_C ≈ 0 (weak rosters) + second hump ~0.3–0.45 (elite rosters).
- **Very high ρ (32):** stronger split — ~48% of teams below L_C=0.05; some teams above 0.5.

**2D — better teams → more congestion at high ρ**
- Low ρ: tight cloud (ability ~0.5, L_C ~0.15).
- ρ=8, 32: upward tail — high-ability teams drift to high L_C (the diagonal he sketched).

That is the model-internal read: **ρ controls how heterogeneous team congestion is across the league**, not just how the selection curve bends.

The slides are built in the same format as your other Phase B characterization decks (left column = setup + readout, right = figure, footer = claim).

## Open this deck

**`3-Master_Plan/re_entry/HEROs_and_PASSes/slides/auto/CHAR_lc_congestion_characterization_AUTO.pptx`**

Two slides, using your `_pd16` PNGs (team L_C, θ ≈ 0.804).

---

### Slide 1 — 1D histogram (# teams vs team L_C)

**Left column:** PD16 Sketch A setup — team L_C formula, ρ arms, diagnostic-only (no score/select), numeric readout (std and tail fractions at ρ=8 and 32).

**Readout bullets:**
- Low ρ → one narrow spike (~L_C ≈ 0.15); teams look alike
- High ρ → split: mass near L_C ≈ 0 (weak rosters) + second hump at high L_C (elite rosters)
- Near-zero ρ matches low-ρ arms (Alex Q1 intuition)

**Footer claim:** ρ controls how heterogeneous team congestion is across the league — not just whether the selection curve bends.

---

### Slide 2 — 2D heatmap (team mean A vs L_C)

**Left column:** Same setup + how to read the heatmap panels.

**Readout bullets:**
- Low ρ → compact blob; ability and congestion barely co-vary
- High ρ → diagonal cloud; elite teams face more peer pressure
- Bridge to Pass C: high ρ creates heterogeneous environments → inverted-U vs pool mean

**Footer claim:** At high ρ, better teams systematically face more congestion — gives ρ a model-internal meaning beyond “the Pass C plot moved.”

---
